llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it claims (fetch WeChat articles and manage an MP backend session) but has configuration/credential and dependency mismatches that are unexplained and merit caution.

dimensions.detail: The code and docs align with the stated purpose: it fetches article pages, optionally falls back to a local Playwright browser, and can use MP backend endpoints (searchbiz, appmsgpublish) when given a session. However the skill reads environment variables (WECHAT_MP_COOKIE, WECHAT_MP_TOKEN) and expects Playwright/WebKit at runtime even though the registry metadata declares no required environment variables or binaries — this is an incoherence between metadata and implementation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and SKILL.md are consistent with the code: they direct the agent to parse article URLs, fetch HTML, optionally use a local Playwright WebKit fallback, perform search/list operations against mp.weixin.qq.com when a session is available, and manage a local session file. All network calls are to WeChat MP endpoints; there are no hidden external endpoints or generic data-exfiltration steps in the provided code or docs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only style), but the shipped code calls Playwright and expects a local WebKit — a runtime dependency not declared in the registry metadata. That mismatch can cause runtime failures; it is not directly a supply-chain redirection, but it is a practical/operational surprise.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code reads WECHAT_MP_COOKIE and WECHAT_MP_TOKEN from environment (session_store.load_session_from_env) and will persist session data (cookie/token) to local cache files (scripts/cache/session.json and login-state.json). The registry metadata declared no required env vars or primary credential. Requiring or using sensitive MP credentials without declaring them is a meaningful misalignment and a privacy/security concern that users should be aware of.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does persist its own session and state to files under its scripts/cache directory (session.json, login-state.json, account_cache.json). always:false (not force-included) and it does not modify other skills or system-wide agent config. Persisting session cookies locally is expected for this feature but increases the attack surface (sensitive cookies on disk).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement a WeChat Official Account article fetcher and backend-session manager, but it reads sensitive environment variables (WECHAT_MP_COOKIE, WECHAT_MP_TOKEN) and writes session cookies/tokens to local files even though the registry metadata lists no required env vars. Before installing, consider: 1) only install if you trust the code owner and are comfortable a skill will store WeChat MP cookies/tokens on disk (scripts/cache/session.json and login-state.json); 2) run in an isolated environment (container or sandbox) if you plan to use real MP credentials; 3) explicitly set or avoid the WECHAT_MP_* env vars depending on whether you want backend-mode functionality; 4) ensure Playwright + WebKit are available on the host (the skill falls back to Playwright and will fail if not present); and 5) if you need stronger assurance, review the full Python files locally or run the scripts manually to observe behavior before granting agent autonomous use.
